body: A study surveys 2034 Australians to place a dollar value on preserving the Kakadu Conservation Zone and finds benefits far exceeding costs. Critics argue that survey answers may not reflect true preferences: respondents have had little time to think, may worry about the interviewer’s opinion, or may enjoy seeing themselves as virtuous. Using the material of the course, how could one assess whether the survey results reflect true preferences? Which preference axioms might the answers violate, how might a survey be designed to detect such violations, and what should be done if they are found?
